scenario: AITA for giving my girlfriend pointers on how to cook better? | So my girlfriend is pissed at me and has a cooking "strike" because, and I quote,"if you are so much better than me at cooking you can do it yourself". We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. After all she cant get better if she doesnt know that something is off. I would tell her whenever she used too little salt or too much spice, if something was a little burnt or undercooked, told her when I knew how to make the dish better next time etc. I would always eat all of it and say thank you so it was not like I was being rude about it. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I need to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. The user is asking if they're "AITA" (Am I the Asshole) for giving their girlfriend cooking tips. Let me break this down step by step.

First, the scenario: They've been together for 2 years, moved in together 6 months ago. They agreed she would cook because she gets home earlier. She's not terrible, but her cooking isn't up to his standards. He started giving her pointers, like too little salt, too much spice, things being burnt or undercooked, and how to improve next time. He always ate everything and said thanks, so he wasn't being rude. Then, when his mom visited, he mentioned she could give his girlfriend cooking advice. His girlfriend seemed fine at the time but later got angry, accused him of humiliating her in front of his family, and now she's on a cooking strike. He apologized but she's still upset.

So, the question is: Is it morally acceptable for him to give her constructive criticism about her cooking?

I think the key points here are about how he gave the advice and the context in which he did it. He started giving pointers when they moved in together, which seems helpful. He didn't complain or throw food away, so he was trying to be supportive. However, when his mom came over, he suggested she give advice, which might have made his girlfriend feel uncomfortable or embarrassed, especially in front of his family.

Constructive criticism can be helpful, but it's important how it's delivered. If she felt that he was constantly pointing out flaws, even if he was trying to help, it could come across as criticism rather than support. Also, bringing in his mom to give advice might have added pressure or made her feel judged, especially in front of someone else.

Another angle is about the agreement they had. She was supposed to cook because she got home earlier, and he was on board with that. But if her cooking wasn't up to his standards, maybe he should have found another way to handle it without making her feel inadequate. Maybe he could have cooked more himself or found a compromise without criticizing her skills.

He mentions that she's overreacting, but it's possible that she felt undermined or that her efforts weren't appreciated. Even if he didn't mean to, the way he gave advice might have come off as more critical than supportive, especially in front of his mom.

So, considering all this, I think the action of giving constructive criticism in this context might have crossed a line, especially when involving his mom. It's important to consider how the advice is received and the emotional impact it has on the other person. Therefore, the action might be morally unacceptable because it led to hurt feelings and a breakdown in their agreement.
